subject: history_social
passage: Farming in ancient Egypt depended on the yearly flood of the Nile River, which spread water and rich soil across the fields. To track the flood, officials used nilometers: stone staircases or pillars marked with measured levels. A flood that reached the right height usually meant a large harvest, so officials used the readings to ______ how much grain farmers would grow and to set taxes accordingly.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The flood came before the harvest, and its height "usually meant" a certain kind of harvest. Officials could therefore use the readings to judge in advance how much grain would be grown. Judging something ahead of time is predicting it, so "predict" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The harvest had not happened yet when the flood was measured, so there was nothing to remember.
explanation.B: Correct. Because the flood level signaled what the harvest would be, officials used it to predict, or estimate in advance, how much grain farmers would grow.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Officials "used the readings" to set taxes, so they paid close attention to the harvest estimate rather than ignoring it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text describes a practical use of the readings, setting taxes, not a celebration.
